Learned Additional Public Prosecutor would submit that as directed by the Court,
notice was taken to the victim as required U/s.15- A(3) of the Special Act.
But, it could not be served, as the victim refused to receive the notice.
Proof of service is filed along with the affidavit of the concerned police officers.
None appeared for the victim, though she was intimated as mentioned above, offered notice as per law.
No objections filed for the victim, opposing the application inspite of opportunity.

Petitioner is the sole Accused in S.C.No.49/S/2024 on the file of the learned Special Judge For Speedy Trial of Cases under SCs/STs (PoA) Amendment Act-2015-cum-IV Addl.District & Sessions Judge, Guntur.

sentences.text: Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner would submit that petitioner/appellant was convicted for the offence U/s.376(2)(a)(i), 417, 506 IPC and U/s.3(2)(va) of SCs/STs (PoA) Amendment Act, 2015.

Accordingly, he was sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten (10) years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- (Rupees One Thousand only) and in default suffer simple imprisonment for a period of six (06) months for the offence U/s.376(2)(a)(i) IPC.

Further, the petitioner was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of one (01)
year and to pay fine of Rs.500/- (Rupees Five Hundred only) and in default, suffer simple imprisonment for a period of three (03) months for the offence U/s.417 IPC.

Further, the petitioner was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of one (01)
year and to pay fine of Rs.500/- (Rupees Five Hundred only) and in default, suffer simple imprisonment for a period of three (03) months for the offence U/s.506 IPC.
Further, the petitioner was sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten (10) years for the offence U/s.3(2)(va) of SCs/STs (PoA) Amendment Act, 2015.
All the sentences shall run concurrently.

The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner/appellant would submit that the petitioner paid the fine amount as ordered by the learned trial Court and receipt has been filed along with the appeal grounds.
He would further submit that as per the case of prosecution, the petitioner and the victim were in relationship for some time and that the appellant promised to marry the victim.
Later, the appellant committed breach of promise and refused to marry the victim.
Therefore, the victim presented a report to police.
Police investigated the case and filed charge sheet before the learned Special Court.

sentences.text: He would further submit that the learned trial Court convicted the petitioner for the offence U/s.417 IPC for the breach of the alleged promise.
But, surprisingly, convicted the petitioner for the offence U/s.376(2)(a)(i) IPC also, which is contrary to the judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

Therefore,
the petitioner/appellant filed the appeal, challenging the impugned judgment of the learned Special Court on various grounds, including the question of law, on conviction for the offence U/s.376(2)(a)(i) IPC.

He would further submit that the petitioner was lodged In Central Prison,
Nellore, since 19.01.2026.
The learned Senior Counsel would further submit that the maximum sentence of imprisonment imposed in the case is 10 years, which is a fixed sentence.
The petitioner has fair chance to succeed in the appeal.
There is no possibility of hearing the appeal in the coming days.
Considering all the above stated circumstances, the order of sentence of imprisonment imposed by the learned Special Court may be suspended, pending disposal of the appeal.
Learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed the application, submitting that it is not a fit case to suspend the sentence.
However , no written objections were filed, opposing the application or stating the grounds in detail.
No objections were also filed for the victim, as already stated above.

Considering the above submissions of both sides, and the fact that the sentence of imprisonment imposed in the case is a fixed sentence of ten (10) years and as there is no possibility of hearing appeal in the near future, this Court is of the considered opinion that "the order of sentence of imprisonment alone imposed by the learned Special Judge For Speedy Trial of Cases under SCs/STs (PoA) Amendment Act-2015- cum-IV Addl.District & Sessions Judge, Guntur, vide judgment dated 19.01.2026 passed in S.C.No.49/S/2024 against the petitioner/app ellant be suspended, and the petitioner/appellant shall be released on bail subject to the following conditions":
i) The petitioner/appellant/Accused shall be enlarged on bail, on executing a personal bond for Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only), with two (02)
sureties for a like sum each, to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
ii) On such release, the petitioner/appellant/Accused shall appear before the learned trial Court, on every fourth Saturday of the month, till disposal of the Appeal.
